# Self-study {.unnumbered}

<!-- This file is the source of a page on the course website. Read it there: https://ai.buas.nl/open-courses/introduction-to-ml/self-study/00_overview.html -->

Self-study teaches the concepts of machine learning in six themes. Each theme is a short series of activities: notebooks that you run and complete, and pages that you read or try out in your browser. The notebooks use small public datasets, such as the Palmer penguins and California housing prices, so that you can focus on one concept at a time.

Work through the activities of a theme in order. The [course route](../course-guide.qmd#the-course-route) shows when to study each theme.

## At a glance

| Theme | You learn |
|------|------------------------------|
| [1](theme-1/00_overview.qmd) | What machine learning is, how to train classification, regression and clustering models with scikit-learn, and the stages of a machine-learning project |
| [2](theme-2/00_overview.qmd) | How to prepare and explore data, and how to avoid leakage and distribution shift |
| [3](theme-3/00_overview.qmd) | How to evaluate, compare and tune models, and how linear regression, logistic regression and clustering work |
| [4](theme-4/00_overview.qmd) | Pipelines and the ColumnTransformer: preprocessing and model in one object |
| [5](theme-5/00_overview.qmd) | Decision trees, random forests and gradient boosting |
| [6](theme-6/00_overview.qmd) | How to communicate technical work, read machine-learning research and test its ideas |
